summary.text: Dina Titus is the Democratic incumbent for Nevada's 1st Congressional District, which she has represented since 2013 after an earlier term in the House from 2009 to 2011. A political scientist, she taught at UNLV for decades and served in the Nevada Senate, including as minority leader, before entering Congress. Her official biography highlights her work on affordable housing, transportation and nuclear waste policy.

paragraphs.text: Titus was born in Thomasville, Georgia, and grew up in Tifton, Georgia, according to Ballotpedia; her official biography says she grew up in Tifton with her parents and a younger sister. She earned a bachelor's degree from the College of William and Mary, a master's degree from the University of Georgia and a doctorate from Florida State University.

She taught American and Nevada government and political science classes at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, from 1979 until her retirement in 2011. Her official biography describes her as a non-fiction writer known for expertise on the history and policy of nuclear power, weaponry and waste.
Titus served in the Nevada Senate, representing District 7 for 20 years until 2008, and her official biography says she was Senate Minority Leader from 1993 to 2009.

She won election to the U.S. House from Nevada's 3rd District in 2008 and lost re-election in 2010 to Joe Heck by less than one percentage point. She then won the 1st District seat in 2012 and has been re-elected since, including in 2024.

In the 2025-2026 Congress, Titus sits on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, where her official biography says she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee.

The same biography describes her as dean of Nevada's congressional delegation, vice chair of the Hellenic Caucus and a founding member of the Colorado River Caucus. It says she has opposed nuclear waste storage at Yucca Mountain for three decades, introduced legislation to ban bump stocks after the Las Vegas shooting, and played a role in the Brightline West high-speed rail project.

It also says she is addressing the affordable housing crisis in Southern Nevada with legislation to provide more rental housing vouchers and to require large institutional investors to divest homes they have bought there.
Titus has been married to UNLV professor Thomas C. Wright for more than 40 years, according to her official biography.
